claims: Timothée Chalamet faced significant backlash in March 2026 for comments made about ballet and opera.

Timothée Chalamet said "I don't want to be working in ballet or opera, or you know, things where it's like, 'Hey, keep this thing alive,' even though it's like, no one cares about this anymore" during a Feb. 24, 2026, Variety and CNN town hall with Matthew McConaughey, according to People.com.
Opera singer Isabelle Leonard labeled the comments "ineloquent and narrow minded".
Seattle Opera offered a "14%" discount code named "TIMOTHEE" in response.
Conan O'Brien roasted Timothée Chalamet in the opening monologue of the 2026 Oscars, notes The Hollywood Reporter.
Jokes about Timothée Chalamet's comments were made at the 2026 Oscars, notes The Hollywood Reporter.
Fran Drescher defended her "Marty Supreme" costar Timothée Chalamet, as reported by E! News.
Fran Drescher described Timothée Chalamet as a "sweet and kind person" who may have "spoken out of turn," as reported by E! News.
Some observers noted that Timothée Chalamet’s family has ties to the School of American Ballet.
Timothée Chalamet’s comments were meant to be a lighthearted joke about the difficulty of maintaining artistic relevance, notes Forbes.
Page Six published a 56-second YouTube video on Mar 10, 2026 discussing the backlash to Timothée Chalamet's comments.
Louis Levanti published a 49-second YouTube video on Mar 8, 2026 providing another perspective on the controversy.
